payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with the input image, is there visible progress toward closing the woman's jacket, even if it is not fully closed?
node.criteria: Pass: comparing the same front closure in both images shows the panels have moved together or the opening has visibly narrowed, while the jacket is not fully closed. Fail: the closure is sufficiently visible in both images to establish no such change. Do not infer progress or its absence from the changed pose, a flared edge, or drape alone. Unknown: occlusion, pose, or image detail prevents a reliable comparison.
node.binding: Compare the same jacket's front closure in the source and edited images. Account for the edited sideways pose and drape; assess panel alignment and the opening along the closure, not the outer edge. Count only visible progress toward closure.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows the woman turned sideways, and the jacket’s front closure is obscured by the pose and drape. The same closure cannot be reliably compared with the source to establish visible progress toward closing it.

fulfillment: The node’s endpoint check is appropriately strict, but its progress check is too dependent on comparing the same closure when the edited pose obscures it. In these images, the source shows the pink jacket open, while the edited image turns the woman sideways and the front closure is hidden by the jacket’s drape; that supports neither a reliable progress finding nor a negative one. Keep this case unresolved rather than inferring progress from the changed pose or treating obscuration as no progress. For future cases, make the progress criterion assess only visible, attributable evidence of the requested closure change relative to the source, and return unknown when pose, occlusion, or drape prevents that comparison. Preserve the separate fully-closed endpoint and the rubric’s distinction between no progress and insufficient evidence. The trace is valid and queried, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure indicated; the disagreement is evidential uncertainty, not grounds to force the reference label.

response.content: {"text":"The current binding already correctly distinguishes visible progress from pose or drape and returns unknown when the closure cannot be compared. The trace is valid and queried, so this is not a transport, schema, or dependency failure. Do not tune the node to match the aggregate “yes” label: it constrains the overall result, not this check’s atomic truth. In these images the source closure is visible and open, but the edited sideways pose and hanging jacket obscure the closure; the trace therefore supports uncertainty, not a finding of progress or no progress. Preserve the separate fully-closed endpoint and the rubric’s distinction between partial progress, no progress, and insufficient evidence. If refining the typed binding or criteria, clarify that progress requires attributable visible change in the closure itself, while pose, occlusion, and drape alone cannot establish either progress or its absence; keep unknown when comparison is unreliable. Low confidence or repeated variation should prompt investigation, not be treated as evidence that the requested edit is absent."}
